thread:
maya: :rotating_light: Seeing a p99 spike in eu-west for /v1/chat/generate starting ~12:35 UTC. Customers reporting 3-6s p99 (normally ~1s). Stack traces show request queueing on rwd-7b-quant workers around 12:34.

raj: Which customers are impacted? any recent deploys to eu-west? SLOs p95=500ms p99=1200ms for that route right?

maya: Impacted keys: corp-analytics, travelx, searchly (high QPS). No infra deploys in the last 2 hours, but a model rollout to rwd-7b-quant finished ~12:30. SLOs you quoted are correct.

tyler: Looking at infra metrics: instance CPU on GPU nodes holding rwd-7b-quant are fine, but queue depth and blocking time jumped. Likely a KV-cache thrash + long attention kernels for some long-context requests. Quick mitigations: 1) enable circuit breaker to start failing fast for noisy keys, 2) route eu-west traffic for /v1/chat to rwd-3b-fallback (lower quality but much faster), 3) apply soft rate limits to top noisy API keys, 4) if model rollout is suspect, rollback to previous model variant.

alex: I can toggle routing and circuit breaker. Proposed steps I can run now:
- enable-cb --scope=eu-west --route=/v1/chat --p99-threshold=1200ms --fail-open=false
- apply-fallback --route=/v1/chat --region=eu-west --model=rwd-3b-fp16 --weight=100 --reason="p99 spike"
(Using admin CLI, will annotate with incident id)

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-1234 created by alex: "eu-west p99 spike /v1/chat". Pager duty notified.

sarah: I'll contact the three customer leads to set expectations and ask for any unusual payloads (very long prompts, high n, streaming with large chunk sizes). Also collecting a few repro request IDs.

maya: Posting a quick log snippet showing queue depth and kernel latency from 12:33-12:37: 
```
[12:33:21] queue_depth=12 req_id=abc123 model=rwd-7b-quant kernel_ms=8 kv_miss=1
[12:34:02] queue_depth=48 req_id=def456 model=rwd-7b-quant kernel_ms=420 kv_miss=12
[12:34:45] queue_depth=102 req_id=ghi789 model=rwd-7b-quant kernel_ms=980 kv_miss=24
[12:35:10] queue_depth=88 req_id=jkl012 model=rwd-7b-quant kernel_ms=700 kv_miss=18
```

tyler: That kernel_ms spike + kv_miss pattern screams cold/cache-eviction for long prefixes. Two-prong: fallback and CB now; follow-up: increase KV cache size for rwd-7b or tune cache TTLs, and add adaptive batching controls so long requests don't stall short ones.

alex: Executing mitigations now. Commands run: 
- admin toggle-circuit-breaker --scope=eu-west --route=/v1/chat --threshold-p99-ms=1200 --action=reject-heavy-keys --reason="INC-2026-1234"
- admin set-routing --route=/v1/chat --region=eu-west --model=rwd-3b-fp16 --weight=100 --note="temporary fallback for p99 spike"
Responses: circuit-breaker enabled, routing updated -> 100% to rwd-3b-fp16 in eu-west.

maya: Telemetry showing improvement: p99 dropped to ~1.3s within 90s of toggles, p95 stable under 600ms. Queue depth back to single digits. Good signal.

raj: Nice. Can we add a short-term rate-limit rule for corp-analytics/travelx to prevent re-trigger if they retry aggressively? Suggest 20 req/s with token-bucket burst 40 for those orgs.

alex: Applied soft rate limits for corp-analytics and travelx (20rps, burst 40). Rule id: rl-2026-33. Will monitor.

sarah: Customers notified. Two said they had several long-context batch requests at spike time; recommended they chunk requests or use streaming with smaller chunks.

tyler: Action items:
- (tyler) follow up in 30m to decide on rolling fallback weight back to 0 or increasing if needed
- (maya) collect representative long-request payloads and add to repro eval set
- (alex) create a postmortem note and revert CB/routing only after 45m of stable telemetry
- (infra) schedule KV cache TTL increase test and adaptive batching experiment for rwd-7b-quant

maya: I'll keep monitoring. If p99 creeps back up, we'll escalate to full capacity scale or rollback model rollout.

alex: Marking incident INC-2026-1234 as mitigated. Will keep open for postmortem.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-1234 status -> mitigated. Next check in 2026-04-01T13:20:00Z.

raj: Thanks team. Documenting this under playbook notes: we should add an explicit "fallback-to-smaller-model" quick path and RBAC for admin toggles so oncall can act faster.

sarah: +1. Closing customer comms loop after postmortem.

tyler: Closing thread once postmortem doc linked. For now monitoring green. :thumbsup:
